newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Greek oil tanker still aground off Venezuela coast.
newsitem.headline: Greek oil tanker still aground off Venezuela coast.

text.p: Venezuelan port authorities were still trying Thursday to float Greek oil tanker Olympic Sponsor which ran aground in the Gulf of Venezuela four days ago.
"We are still working on it. We're going to take some crude off this afternoon to see if that works," Maracaibo Port Captain Regulo Dominguez told Reuters in a brief telephone interview.

Since the accident, tanker traffic through the Lake Maracaibo navigation channel has been limited to ships with less than 36 feet (11.1 meters) of draught, down from the usual 39 foot six inch (12.2 meters) maximum, he said.
Dominguez said the restriction would remain in place until the Olympic Sponsor had been refloated, despite the fact that the tanker had run aground outside of the channel.

The Olympic Sponsor was en route to Rotterdam with 477,000 barrels of 24 degree API (American Petroleum Institute) crude on board. The port authority has said that no oil has been spilled into the water.
The crude was to be delivered to Germany's Veba Oel AG. PDVSA owns a 50 percent stake in Veba's 225,000 barrels per day Gelsenkirchen refinery in Germany.
The accident took place in virtually the same place as the Greek-flagged Nissos Amorgos tanker grounded Feb. 28 spilling at least 28,000 barrels of heavy crude.
